question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.text: To introduce Gurov by showing how a piece of resort gossip draws his attention to an unfamiliar woman and how he comes to single her out among the new arrivals.
To establish that Gurov, unlike the other visitors at the resort, actively dislikes the company of strangers and prefers to spend his entire holiday at Yalta alone.
To describe the unfamiliar woman's daily routine on the sea-front in careful detail in order to suggest that she has grown unhappy with the companions she brought with her to Yalta.
To compare the social customs of the resort at Yalta with those of Gurov's home city of Moscow.

explanation: The correct answer is A. The passage opens with the resort's gossip about "a new person"—a lady with a dog—then follows Gurov, who has "begun to take an interest in new arrivals," as he notices her and meets her "several times a day," singling her out among the visitors. Introducing Gurov through that growing attention is the passage's purpose. Choice B reverses his attitude, since he is drawn to the new arrivals rather than avoiding them; Choice C invents an unhappiness the text never reports about the woman; and Choice D promises a Yalta-Moscow comparison the passage does not make.
passage:
The following text is from Anton Chekhov's 1899 short story "The Lady with the Dog" (translated by Constance Garnett). Dmitri Gurov is a Moscow banker on holiday at the seaside resort of Yalta.

It was said that a new person had appeared on the sea-front: a lady with a little dog. Dmitri Dmitritch Gurov, who had by then been a fortnight at Yalta, and so was fairly at home there, had begun to take an interest in new arrivals. Sitting in Verney's pavilion, he saw, walking on the sea-front, a fair-haired young lady of medium height, wearing a beret; a white Pomeranian dog was running behind her. And afterwards he met her in the public gardens and in the square several times a day. She was walking alone, always wearing the same beret, and always with the same white dog; no one knew who she was, and every one called her simply "the lady with the dog."
